newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Nov 23 Initial Claims from 342,000; Nov 23 4-Week Average from 336,250; and Nov 16 Continued Claims from 2,417,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast jobless claims filings of 337,000 in the November 30 week.
The department said 13 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended November 23, the latest period for which the data are available.
They included California, with 19,564; Texas, with 12,288; Minnesota, with 3,429; Oregon, with 3,175; North Carolina, with 2,427; and New York with 2,391.

California reported layoffs in the construction industry and in agriculture. Texas attributed its increase to the return to a five-day workweek after a shorter reporting period the previous week. Minnesota had layoffs in the construction industry and in manufacturing.
North Carolina reported layoffs in the service and transportation equipment industries while New York had layoffs in the construction industry. Oregon gave no explanation for its increase.
Ohio was the only state reporting a decrease in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the November 23 week. It provided no reason for the drop of 1,725 in claims.
